extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and institutions applying for American Heart Association research grants (PIs, trainees, mentors, research administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program-specific eligibility/expectations for applying to American Heart Association (AHA) research funding opportunities across predoctoral, postdoctoral, career development, institutional, topic-focused, data science, and registry-research programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-proposal requirement and invited full proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Some programs require pre-proposals, with full proposals by invitation only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must watch the funding opportunity details for whether a pre-proposal is required and for pre-proposal deadlines; only those invited after pre-proposal submission may submit full proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator-initiated research: PI career-stage qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: For investigator-initiated funding, qualification for awards is largely based on the principal investigator’s career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should select investigator-initiated opportunities appropriate to their career level (predoctoral, postdoctoral, early-career, mid-career, senior) and ensure their materials demonstrate suitability for that career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-focused funding aligned to AHA mission and strategic objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic-focused programs support specific areas of science deemed critical to achieving the AHA mission and strategic objectives; some projects may be co-funded with other organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should address the specific scientific priorities described in the program details and may leverage co-funding opportunities; examine program priorities closely to ensure alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Science Grants: global eligibility and career-stage inclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Science Grants fund researchers from anywhere in the world and support investigators at all career stages, from trainees to senior scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants working in data science should confirm the program's topic focus and assemble teams/expertise appropriate to the stated requirements (e.g., causal inference, machine learning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registry Research: use of Quality Programs databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators can submit proposals to conduct research using the Association's Quality Programs databases, which contain millions of patient records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must describe how they will use registry/national-level data and comply with data access, privacy, and analysis requirements described in the registry research opportunity details.

rubrics_metrics.name: AHA Predoctoral Fellowship: enrollment and career-intent requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhances the training of promising students in pre-doctoral or clinical health professional degree training programs who intend careers as scientists, physician-scientists or clinician-scientists, or related careers aimed at improving global health and wellbeing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be enrolled in an eligible pre-doctoral or clinical training program and articulate a clear career trajectory toward research; note program deadline (e.g., August 4, 2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: AHA Postdoctoral Fellowship: non-independent status and mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhances the training of postdoctoral applicants who are not yet independent; the applicant must be embedded in an appropriate investigative group with mentorship, support, and relevant scientific guidance of a research mentor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should demonstrate an appropriate mentor environment, plans for career development, and that the candidate is not yet independent; check specific sponsor-designated collaboration funds when applicable (e.g., AHA/CHF, Autism Speaks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Award for Undergraduate Student Training: institutional responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded to qualified institutions that can offer a meaningful research experience supporting the AHA mission and that encourage undergraduate students from all disciplines to consider research careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional applicants must describe how the program will provide meaningful research experiences, recruitment of diverse undergraduates, and mentorship/training structures (deadline example: Sept. 9, 2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: AHA Institutional Research Enhancement Award (AIREA): eligibility and aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Stimulates research at institutions that provide baccalaureate or advanced degrees related to scientific research training; eligible institutions may not have been major recipients of NIH support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should fund small-scale research projects related to cardiovascular diseases and brain health, enhance the institution's research environment, and expose students to research opportunities (deadline example: Sept. 10, 2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Award: early-first-appointment support
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports highly promising healthcare and academic professionals in the early years of first professional appointment to assure the applicant’s future success as a research scientist in cardiovascular and/or cerebrovascular disease research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be in the early years of their first appointment and provide plans for independent research development, mentorship, and institutional support (deadline example: Dec. 1, 2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Visiting Professorship Award: short-term exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Brings internationally based scientists to the U.S. for one week to foster scientific exchange and expand collaborative opportunities between the Visiting Professor and their U.S.-based host in research aligning with the AHA mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate meaningful scientific exchange and alignment with AHA priorities; note timing/availability varies (proposal deadline for 2026 has passed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative Project Award: novelty and non-duplication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports highly innovative, high-impact research that could lead to critical discoveries or major advancements; the idea proposed should not have been submitted in whole or in part in a previous proposal for AHA support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on transformational, high-risk/high-reward concepts; explicitly state that the proposal (or substantial parts) has not been previously submitted to AHA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ralph L. Sacco Scholarships in Brain Health: scope and applicant type
rubrics_metrics.description: Enables early career trainees to undertake a mentored two-year research project targeting various aspects of brain health; 2026 awards are for MD or PhD applicants in postdoctoral fellowship training with a focus on brain health; projects must focus on prevention with a clear connection to neurological or mental/behavioral health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be in eligible postdoctoral status, propose prevention-focused brain health research, and provide appropriate mentorship and project plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid Impact Research Award: topical alignment and career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: For early- and mid-career investigators proposing innovative studies aligned with sudden cardiac arrest/resuscitation science, Cardiovascular Kidney Metabolic (CKM) Syndrome, or stroke and/or vascular dementias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must align with the specified topical areas and demonstrate innovation appropriate to early- or mid-career investigators; check individual opportunity details for deadlines and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redefining Women’s Health Studio: idea-stage innovation for women’s health
rubrics_metrics.description: Invites researchers, clinicians, entrepreneurs and innovators to submit ideas to advance groundbreaking research and novel solutions in conditions that disproportionately or distinctly impact women’s health; four priority areas are described in program details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should address one of the program’s priority areas and propose innovative solutions; consult program details for priority themes and submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative network awards: multi-site/consortium expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Network/team awards (e.g., Heart Transplantation Research Network, CART Network, SFRN) expect collaborative networks of clinician investigators whose collective research will address specified gaps and enhance patient management or detection/progression research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should describe multidisciplinary collaboration, governance, team roles, and how the network will address the program’s strategic goals; many of these require pre-proposals and have passed deadlines for current cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Science Grants — disciplinary and methodological expertise requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunities specify required multidisciplinary expertise, e.g., teams with expertise in two or more areas such as cardio-oncology, CKM Syndrome, health economics, epidemiology, biostatistics with experience in causal inference methods, machine learning, and cardiovascular research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble teams with complementary domain and data-science skills; highlight experience in causal inference, ML, and cardiovascular applications; provide concrete plans to utilize relevant real-world data sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources and methods encouragement for real-world evidence projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are encouraged to leverage de-identified claims data, electronic health records, and prospective cohort studies when evaluating treatments or prevalence using real-world data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail data provenance, de-identification, analytic methods (including causal inference/ML approaches), and team capacity to handle complex real-world datasets; state data access plans and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: GLP-1 medication effects opportunity: expected expertise and collaborative proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Research focused on evaluating the effects of GLP-1 and/or GIP agonists among individuals with cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic disease and/or obesity should include applicants with experience in causal inference methods, machine learning, and cardiovascular research; collaborative multidisciplinary proposals are encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should justify data sources and analytic strategy, describe multidisciplinary roles, and align the research question with program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application resources and policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should consult the Application Resources page for AHA policies and restrictions, application preparation guidance, and general guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Application Resources to verify eligibility, budget rules, human subjects/IRB policies, and other administrative requirements before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and submission platform holidays
rubrics_metrics.description: Each opportunity has a specified proposal deadline and there are organizational and submission-platform holidays that may affect timing (examples of 2026 AHA and ProposalCentral holidays are listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan submissions around listed deadlines and platform holidays to avoid last-minute issues; contact the applications team if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sponsor-designated collaboration funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain awards include additional collaboration money designated through named partners (e.g., AHA/CHF Congenital Heart Defect Research Awards, Autism Speaks, Barth Syndrome Foundation, California Walnut Commission, Foundation for Sarcoidosis Research, AHA/VIVA Physician Research Award, American Headache Society).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review program details to determine eligibility for collaboration funds and any additional requirements or priorities tied to those funds; cite co-funding sources in the application as required.
